Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The `StringUtils.join(Object[] array, String separator)` method in the `org.apache.commons.lang3` package accepts an array of objects and a separator string. If the array is null, the method returns null immediately without performing any further processing. This behavior aligns with the failing test case where a null value is returned when calling `StringUtils.join(NULL_TO_STRING_LIST)`. 

The current bug report indicates that the `toString` method of one of the objects in the collection returns null, causing a NullPointerException. This is because the `StringUtils.join` method does not handle cases where the `toString` method of an object returns null.

To diagnose the issue step by step:
1. The test case calls `StringUtils.join(NULL_TO_STRING_LIST)`, where one of the objects in the list has a `toString` method returning null.
2. Inside `StringUtils.join(Object[] array, String separator)`, the method simply returns null if the input array is null, without iterating over the elements in the array.
3. Since one of the objects in `NULL_TO_STRING_LIST` has a `toString` method returning null, when `join` attempts to concatenate the strings, a NullPointerException is thrown.

The root cause of the issue is that `StringUtils.join` does not handle cases where the `toString` method of objects in the array returns null, leading to a NullPointerException when trying to concatenate the strings.

Shall I proceed to provide the methods to be fixed to address this issue?

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
